sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and logger setup
sections.what: Loads the libraries, settings and helper classes this file uses, and sets up a logger for it.
sections.why: Brings in the tools for splitting text, storing vectors and reading settings.

sections.name: VectorStoreManager (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up the store and text splitter
sections.what: Prepares a manager for one named collection and a splitter that cuts text into pieces of set size with overlap. It then opens or creates the store: ChromaDB opens a folder on disk, while FAISS is only marked empty until documents are added.
sections.why: Chunks keep each piece small enough for the embedding model, and overlap keeps context across cuts.
sections.watch_out: The FAISS branch never loads a previously saved index, so after a restart searches can return nothing until documents are added again.

sections.name: VectorStoreManager: add_documents
sections.title: Splitting text and saving chunks
sections.what: Cuts each parsed document into chunks, attaches details such as file name, type, page, slide, sheet and chunk position, and writes them into the store. ChromaDB saves right away; FAISS writes its index file to disk. Returns how many chunks were added.
sections.why: Chunk-level details let answers point to the exact location in a source.
sections.watch_out: Every call adds new entries with no duplicate check, so adding the same document twice duplicates its chunks.

sections.name: VectorStoreManager (part 3)
sections.title: Finding the closest matching chunks
sections.what: Asks the store for the most similar chunks to a question, with an optional metadata filter and optional minimum score, and returns each one with its content, metadata and score. Returns an empty list if no store is loaded.
sections.why: The store finds relevant text by meaning rather than exact words.
sections.watch_out: Scores are empty unless a threshold is given, and score scales can differ between stores, so one threshold may not suit both.

sections.name: VectorStoreManager: delete_collection
sections.title: Deleting a collection and reporting stats
sections.what: Deletes the saved folder for this collection and clears the in-memory store. A second method reports how many chunks ChromaDB holds, or only the store type for FAISS.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user start a collection over and check how much it holds.
sections.watch_out: Deletion is permanent, with no backup or confirmation step.

summary: Manages the store that holds document pieces as numbers so the app can find text by meaning, and it cuts documents into chunks before storing them.
purpose: Turns parsed documents into searchable chunks, saves them to ChromaDB or FAISS, and returns the closest matches for a question.
why: Likely reason: semantic search needs chunks small enough for the embedding model, and a store that persists between runs.
how: The manager is created for one collection and prepares a text splitter. create_vector_store opens or creates the store. add_documents splits each document, attaches metadata, and writes the chunks, saving to disk. search finds the closest chunks with an optional filter and minimum score. delete_collection removes the saved folder. get_stats reports the count.
inputs: Parsed documents from the parser layer, a question and result count for search, optional metadata filter and score threshold, and settings for chunk size, overlap, store type and storage path.
outputs: A count of chunks added, a list of matches each with content, metadata and score, a stats dictionary, and files written under the storage path.
risks: The FAISS branch never reloads a saved index, and adding documents when none is loaded creates a fresh index that overwrites the saved one, so a second indexing run may erase earlier content. The persist call may not exist in newer ChromaDB versions. delete_collection and force_new delete data permanently. The folder filter may not be supported by the store's metadata filter.
debug: If search returns nothing, check the logs for vector store not initialized and confirm the store type in settings. If FAISS results disappear after a restart or a second run, check for the overwrite risk. If add_documents fails on a chromadb version error, check the persist call. Verify the storage folder under the configured vector store path.
